h font size.
- Steps the font size down from the theme's default, one point at a time, until the summed label advances (`Font.get_string_size`) fit the remaining room (`get_viewport_rect().size.x`).
- Applies the resulting size as a per-button font-size override, and only if a reduction was actually needed — a HUD that already fits is left alone.

Font stepping is coarse (16→15 removes ~6% of the text width), so the row typically lands ~50px clear of the edge rather than exactly on it, which also absorbs any small discrepancy in my padding/size accounting.

I deliberately did **not** use `clip_text`. It looks like the obvious lever, but on a `Button` it also collapses the button's minimum width to its padding — a `BoxContainer` sizes non-expanding children to their minimum, so the row would shrink to ~236px and every label would be clipped. That would trade clipped buttons for clipped text. Shrinking the font keeps every label fully readable, just slightly smaller.

## Residual uncertainty

The one thing I could not confirm empirically is whether `get_theme_stylebox("normal").get_minimum_size().x` is exactly the padding Godot adds to a `Button`'s minimum width. If it's off by more than the font-step slack (~60px across the row), the row could still exceed 1280 by a small amount. If you can run `cd godot_project && godot --headless --quit-after 60`, that would settle it — the change is self-correcting for any font metrics, but it isn't proof against a wrong padding assumption.
